subject: POC success criteria and evaluation plan — Veridian Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Recap: POC goals & proposed success criteria

Thanks for the call today, Emma and Tom — good alignment across the team. Summarizing the POC scope and proposed success criteria so we can lock the plan and owners. Please flag anything missing or off.

POC objective:
- Validate Redwood Inference can meet Veridian's production SLOs for the clinical summarization pipeline and demonstrate unit economics across our typical workload.

Proposed 6-week POC (see attached POC_SOW_v1.pdf and latency_test_plan.xlsx):
Week 0 (kickoff): data exchange, account provisioning, sign SOW
Week 1: integration of ingestion + inference (sample dataset, API keys, minimal pipeline)
Week 2: baseline measurements (cold-start and steady-state)
Week 3: optimization (batching, caching, quantization where acceptable)
Week 4: targeted stress tests (throughput/scale)
Week 5: quality evaluation and human review scoring
Week 6: wrap, findings, go/no-go decision and pricing conversation

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 400 ms for 512-token requests with resident prefix cache enabled
- Throughput: sustained 3k tokens/sec end-to-end for the summarization pipeline under expected arrival pattern (bursty during EHR sync windows)
- Cost: effective cost <= $0.0009 per token for steady-state traffic (after batching/caching knobs)
- Quality: human-rated mean score >= 4.0/5 on a 200-sample holdout set for fidelity and clinical safety checks; automated semantic-similarity >= 0.87 on the same set

Ownership:
- Marissa (me): commercial lead, SOW sign-off, timeline coordination
- Neha: technical onboarding, integration checklist, run initial baselines
- Dev: benchmark harness and stress tests, ingests test dataset and shares telemetry
- Veridian: Emma/Tom provide sample dataset, target list of 200 evaluation prompts, and procurement contacts for SOW signature

Next steps (please by EOD Thu):
1) Confirm you agree to the 6-week timeline above or propose adjustments
2) Approve success criteria or suggest edits/weights for tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality)
3) Provide the procurement contact and preferred PO/SOW process

Attachments: POC_SOW_v1.pdf, latency_test_plan.xlsx

Thanks — ready to kick off as soon as we have signatures and the sample dataset.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals & proposed success criteria

Adding technical detail and a few constraints from the infra/benchmark side so expectations are clear.

Measurement methodology:
- Workload: we'll run a replay of the sample dataset through the ingestion pipeline with the distribution you shared; please include typical sequence lengths and a 95th percentile size estimate.
- Latency measurement: p50/p95 measured at the API gateway (end-to-end) including network and queuing; we will also capture model-server internal decoding times. Warm-up period of 10 minutes before steady-state.
- Throughput: measured as tokens/sec observed at service edge; will run sustained and burst tests.
- Cost/token: we'll report both raw GPU cost estimate and Redwood billable token units with current configuration.

Tech notes and recommendations:
- Model: recommend starting with the open LLM variant noted in the SOW (quantization-enabled x86-optimized build). If you need stricter latency, we can run on dedicated low-latency profiles (smaller batch windows, pinned GPUs).
- Batch sizing and KV caching: we will tune batching and leverage prefix caching for repeated patient context to meet latency/cost targets.
- Test harness: Dev will provide step-by-step scripts (see latency_test_plan.xlsx) to reproduce the runs. We'll collect:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, and cost estimates per 1M tokens

Quality evaluation plan:
- Veridian to provide 200 labeled prompts plus a 200-sample blind holdout.
- Automated metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine) and token-level overlap for regression checks.
- Human review: 5 clinical annotators from your side or ours (TBD), rating summaries for fidelity and safety. Acceptance requires mean >=4.0/5 and no critical safety failures in the holdout.

Risks / caveats:
- If sample prompts contain PHI we need a secure upload mechanism (we can accept S3 with customer-side encryption or a VPC/private deployment).
- Quantization can affect some safety/precision edge cases; we will flag any regression in the quality step and propose mitigation (higher precision profile for those requests).

I'll own the integration checklist and run the baseline tests; Dev will run the stress harness in week 4.

-Neha

Thanks Marissa and Neha — this is very thorough and helpful. A few clarifications from Veridian before we sign the SOW: 

1) Data privacy: the dataset will include limited PHI. We prefer S3 upload with customer-side encryption or VPC peering. Can Redwood confirm both are supported for the POC?
2) Success criteria weighting: we care most about quality > cost > latency. If you had to prioritize tuning knobs, please note which we'd sacrifice first to improve quality.
3) Timeline: our internal review favors a 6-week timeline (we want more time for clinical annotator scheduling). Are you ok moving to 6 weeks instead of 4?
4) Procurement: procurement lead is Michael Harper (michael.harper@veridianhealth.com). He will handle PO and countersignature.

If possible, could you send a brief one-page acceptance criteria matrix (pass/fail + how measured) that we can circulate to clinical leadership? That will speed approvals.

Emma Jones
Director, Clinical Informatics, Veridian Health
